A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Aurora research work and complete 24-page material, including Appendices A and B. Text and rendered-page comparison establish that the scientific content is identical, with only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp visibly changed.

before.justification: v2 reports original serving experiments measuring acceptance length and throughput, including online adaptation, synchronization and loss ablations, and frontier-model evaluations in Sections 4–6 and Appendix B.3.

after.justification: v4 retains the same original experimental results in Sections 4–6 and Appendix B.3. These include measured adaptation trajectories and throughput comparisons against static or no-speculation baselines.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain identical architecture, asynchronous updates, tree attention, acceptance/discard training objectives, and synchronization procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five-domain prompt collection, ordered and mixed traffic scenarios, and held-out frontier-model evaluations. No dataset, domain, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The no-speculation and static-speculator baselines, scratch and pretrained Aurora configurations, and KL/NTP/discard variants remain identical within the corresponding comparisons in Figures 3–10 and Tables 1, 4, and 5.

E3.justification: Request-stream construction, evaluation metrics, batch sizes, lookahead settings, warm-up exclusions, and held-out evaluation procedures are unchanged. The experimental settings documented in Appendix B also match.

E4.justification: The synchronization-frequency study, objective and discard-token ablations, top-k comparison, longer-lookahead analysis, and batch-size sensitivity study retain the same questions and evidence in Sections 4.2 and 5.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including the P05/P50/P95 throughput summaries in Tables 1, 4, and 5. Neither version adds seed information, repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals, or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: All plotted results, numerical entries, and reported findings match. For example, Table 1 retains batch-size-1 speedups of 1.57× for MiniMax M2.1 and 1.51× for Qwen3-Coder-Next; Appendix Tables 4–5 are also identical.

T1.justification: The acceptance and speedup expressions, training-loss formulation, and appendix data and memory definitions are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified training and serving, day-0 deployment, traffic adaptation, infrastructure savings, and algorithm generality, including the stated speedups.

C2.justification: Both versions preserve the same interpretations of synchronization overhead, limited discard-token benefits, and larger gains with longer lookahead. The discussion of diminishing throughput benefits and slowdown at large batch sizes is also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B retain identical RPC implementation, GPU allocation, hardware, optimizer, learning-rate, precision, and batching details. The stated website and model/data access references are unchanged.

R1.justification: All 38 references and their associated discussion match. Positioning relative to Online Speculative Decoding and asynchronous RL systems in Sections 2.2–2.3 is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 3 April 2026 to v4 dated 15 May 2026. This is a limited header-text update; the visible byline, prose, terminology, and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: All ten figures and five tables retain identical graphics, captions, structure, and placement. Rendered pages 2–24 are pixel-identical; the first-page difference is confined to the version/date text.

improvement.justification: The visible revision only updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific arguments, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and presentation throughout the main text and appendices are unchanged, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
